body.title: `mr note create` and `mr note draft create`: `--attach` silently drops a body piped on stdin
body.description:
### Checklist

- [ ] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: 1.126.0. Not the latest (v1.128.0), but the code that causes this is unchanged on `main` at 8f4ff7e317a49a7522a7b4b3c3f5434edd3b4090 (see Possible fixes).
- [x] Operating system and version: macOS (Darwin 25.6.0 arm64)
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? gitlab.com
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues

### Summary

When `--attach` is passed to `glab mr note draft create` (or `glab mr note create`) and the body is piped on stdin, glab uploads the files and creates the comment with only the attachment links. The piped body is dropped without any warning or error, and the command exits 0.

The help says "a comment with only `--attach` neither prompts nor reads a body from stdin". That makes sense when an attachment is read from stdin (`--attach -`), but the body is also ignored when every attachment is a file path, so the stdin body is lost.

### Environment

- OS: Darwin 25.6.0 arm64
- SHELL: /bin/zsh, command run by an agent through non-interactive `bash -c` (stdin is a pipe, not a TTY)
- TERM: dumb
- GLAB: glab 1.126.0 (4dd0d32d1)

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
glab mr note draft create <iid> --file path/to/file.ts --line 10:12 \
  --attach ./a.png --attach ./b.png <<'BODY'
This text should be the comment body.
BODY
```

Then read the draft back:

```shell
glab mr note draft list <iid> -F json | jq -r '.[] | select(.id==<draft-id>) | .note'
```

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

The draft body contains only the attachment links:

```
![a](/uploads/<hash>/a.png)
![b](/uploads/<hash>/b.png)
```

The command prints the new draft ID and exits 0, so nothing tells the user the body was dropped.

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

If no `--attach` value is `-`, glab should read the body from stdin as it does without `--attach`, and append the attachment links to it. If stdin cannot be read because an attachment uses it (`--attach -`) while a body is also expected, glab should fail with an error instead of creating a comment without the body.

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

Workaround used: `glab mr note draft update <iid> <draft-id>` with the body on stdin, pasting the existing upload links into the body.

### Possible fixes

Stdin is skipped whenever any `--attach` is given, not only when an attachment is read from stdin:

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/8f4ff7e317a49a7522a7b4b3c3f5434edd3b4090/internal/commands/mr/note/draft/create/create.go#L137-140
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/8f4ff7e317a49a7522a7b4b3c3f5434edd3b4090/internal/commands/mr/note/mr_note_create.go#L209-210

`mr note update` and `mr note draft update` use the same `len(o.attach) == 0` check before reading stdin:

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/8f4ff7e317a49a7522a7b4b3c3f5434edd3b4090/internal/commands/mr/note/draft/update/update.go#L129-130
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/8f4ff7e317a49a7522a7b4b3c3f5434edd3b4090/internal/commands/mr/note/mr_note_update.go#L138-139

Only skip stdin when an attachment is read from stdin, for example `!slices.Contains(o.attach, "-")` instead of `len(o.attach) == 0`.

The bundled `glab` skill says `draft create` takes "the same `--reply`, `--file`, `--line`, `--old-line`, `-m`, and stdin body options" as `mr note create`, which makes this easy for agents to run into.

body.title: Reduce CI pipeline time spent on Go cache restore and save
body.description:
## Problem

In MR pipelines, most of the time in the Go jobs goes to restoring and saving the cache, not to running the jobs. Timings from pipeline https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/pipelines/2961140219 (13m11s, critical path `tests:unit` → `build_test`):

| Job | Restore cache | Actual work | Save cache |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests:unit` | 3m19s | 37s | 3m58s |
| `tests:integration` | 2m50s | 15s | 3m27s |
| `lint` | 4m30s | 2m12s | 2m12s, then failed (`no space left on device`) |
| `check_docs_update` | 2m17s | 2s | 2m18s |

The cache is large because of file count: about 60k files in `.go/pkg/mod` (a fresh `go mod download` gives about 24.5k, because Go never prunes old module versions) and about 125k files in `.gocache`.

## Tasks

1. Use `pull` (not `pull-push`) for the Go cache in MR pipelines, and keep `pull-push` on `main`. MR pipelines then only get a warm cache if they can read the one `main` writes, so turn off "Use separate caches for protected branches" or otherwise share the key.
2. Fix the `lint` cache: saving it fails with `no space left on device`, so it hasn't been refreshed since 2026-10-09.
3. Make cache restore faster: fastzip/zstd, and stop caching `.go/pkg/mod` or prune it.
4. Cap the cache size so it never needs a manual "Clear runner caches". Add an `after_script` to `.go-cache` that removes `.go/pkg/mod` and `.gocache` when together they exceed a threshold. The runner saves the cache after `after_script`, so the next save starts small, at the cost of one cold run. Pick the threshold so that an unpacked cache still leaves room on the runner disk for the image pull. Optionally add the Go version to the key (`cache:key:files: [.tool-versions]`) so a Go upgrade also resets it.

   Since 2026-11-05 22:09 every `tests:unit` job on `go-tests-unit-1-non_protected` has failed with `runner_system_failure`. The unpacked cache fills the disk, and the following `golang` image pull fails with `no space left on device`, for example https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/jobs/17809453921 (from https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4329). Clearing the runner caches unblocks MRs until the cache grows back.

## Expected result

Task 1 alone should bring an MR pipeline like the one above from about 13m down to about 9–9.5m, with `lint` as the new critical path. These figures are estimates from the job logs and haven't been measured.

body.title: CI: fix lint cache save failing with no space left on device
body.description:
The `lint` job fails to save its cache:

```
FATAL: write ../../../cache/gitlab-org/cli/<hash>/archive_635336076: no space left on device
Failed to create cache
```

The cache being restored was last modified 2026-10-09, so `golangci-lint` analyses more each day as the cache goes staler (the lint step itself took 2m12s).

Options:
- Drop `.gocache` from lint's cache paths and keep only `.golangci-lint-cache` (lint's `.gocache` alone is about 127k files).
- Use a runner with more disk for the cache-saving `main` pipeline.

Pipeline: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/pipelines/2961140219
